10/5 best game i played so far

ARC Raiders is an amazing game where:
• The enemies are smart
• The guns feel great
• The map is beautiful
• And every player you meet is your best friend for exactly 12 seconds

You’ll wave at someone, loot together, fight robots side by side…
then get shot in the back at extraction like it’s a trust-building exercise.

This game taught me:

Never turn your back

Never loot first

Never believe crouch-spamming means “friendly”

And never ask “was that a footstep?” because yes, it was 💀

10/10 gameplay
10/10 sound design
0/10 emotional damage resistance

Would absolutely get betrayed again.

The server stability in this game is atrocious, it lags way too excessively and constant, I've been playing for around 200 hours and the servers have not gotten any better. Considering how much time and grinding it takes to obtain weapons, losing all of it because I lagged in front of a wasp is awful and should never happen.

Vaulting over anything in this game is extremely inconsistent, and buggy, with the character just jumping instead of vaulting. The community is extremely toxic, with many players just backstabbing and taking cheap shots 90% of the time, coupled with the fact that sound design in this game is so awful you cannot hear footsteps from other raiders that are farther than 2 feet away from you, even when they're running right at you. The balancing in this game is solely centered around nerfing everything that is great to give you fewer and fewer options on what to use, especially against arcs. The end game is severely lacking and incomplete, since once you max out all the stations there's literally no other use for the big arc cells.  Every new somewhat big event or update the toxicity in this game gets much worse. Spawning over 10 minutes late makes any map condition not worth doing, since it's just best to immediately extract which is very tedious. There's very few great guns in this game, almost all of them are too expensive to use, or too weak. The shading is way too excessive, with any building you're more than 10 feet away from becoming pitch black from the outside, which makes camping extractions trivially easy. To repeat an earlier point, the player footsteps is atrociously bad, you can barely ever hear footsteps in a game where people love to sneak up on you to kill you before you can react, this really needs to be fixed. A lot of the recent updates have been very lacking, way too slow and adding next to nothing interesting, which makes me worry they will barely add content to this game to then ditch it to make a new game. Expeditions are not worth really doing, only getting a permanent additional 12 stash space and 5 skill points is awful, this is not worth doing considering how you lose all your blueprints, which is an extremely tedious shore to get most of them and the drop chance keeps getting nerfed/reduced. The woke "Body 1" and "Body 2" is also very cringy.

There's no point in getting a legendary weapon, even when you actively avoid fighting people, and even in purely PVE lobbies, the moment you get a legendary weapon every rat tries to kill you to in the most cowardly ways imaginable, not even giving you a chance to fight back. 

The biggest problems of this game is that it is not worth investing too much into anything. Why invest so much time and effort into a strong loadout just to be shot from the back or being stunned by a trap, without ever even having the smallest chance to fight back? The community here is so manipulative and toxic that it's not worth helping people, nor working together to fight the matriarch and queen. 

My best recommendation is to just not buy this garbage game, wait several years until they actually add content, not just meaningless small map conditions.

When it first launched, resource gathering felt like the primary objective, while PvP was secondary. You'd spend a lot of time scavenging for materials and completing missions, and it wasn't uncommon for other teams to cooperate with you. Sometimes strangers would help you find objectives or complete missions together. Of course, there were always a few Rust-style players who would drop in with disposable gear and shoot you on sight, or betray you after pretending to be friendly.

As the game has been out longer, however, most players have already completed the missions and collections. Because of that, the community dynamic has changed significantly. These days, encounters are far more PvP-focused, and the cooperative spirit that made earlier matches memorable is much rarer. Now it feels like the majority of players are those same Rust-style opportunists looking for a fight rather than an adventure.

The game itself is still fun, but the player-driven experience feels very different from what it was during the early days.

First impressions of this game present amazingly well, but it quickly loses it's luster once you realize: 

(1) the Arcs are actually not very threatening, 
(2) inventory management is absolutely awful, 
(3) because blueprints are so rare the crafting system fails to be engaging for most of your time; and,
(4) the skill tree is almost entirely useless.

Ontop of all that, the progression system is literally you just restarting your progress from scratch. You lose all your blueprints, all your crafting benches, all your skill points and your entire inventory. 

What do you gain? An asbolutely useless couple of extra inventory slots.

It's absolute nonsense.

Which is shame, because there's probably a game of the decade hidden in there somewhere.
